payload.title: What Are the Ukrainian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
protect_keywords: wedding superstitions (old URL; SEO to quantify)
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a generous budget, often with a Ukrainian-Australian partner or parent, who want to understand each Ukrainian custom in the order it happens, which belong to the Orthodox or Greek Catholic service and which are family folk custom, and how to carry them into a wedding in Australia or another destination, since Smartraveller advises Australians not to travel to Ukraine.
payload.goal: Read the free Wedded Wonderland digital magazine (primary CTA); secondary, in-context invitation to speak with a Wedded Advisor placed after the 'bringing the customs to your wedding' section.
payload.angle: Ukrainian weddings are a sequence, not a list of oddities: matchmaking with rushnyky, the engagement, the bride's evening and her vinok, the korovai, the playful vykup, then the church rite where the couple step onto a rushnyk and are crowned, and the bread-and-salt welcome into the celebration. We walk 10 to 12 customs in that order, source the church parts from Ukrainian Catholic and Orthodox church pages (including in Australia) and folk customs from the Internet Encyclopedia of Ukraine and museums, label the rest 'often told', and, because Smartraveller says 'Do not travel' to Ukraine (updated 02 November 2026), show Ukrainian-Australian and mixed-heritage couples how these customs travel to a wedding in Australia or elsewhere, starting with their parish priest.
must_include: One early framing line: the church rite is set by the Church; the folk customs around it vary by family and region
Customs in order, grouped 'Before and at the church' and 'The celebration', each numbered (10 to 12)
The rushnyk as the thread through the day (matchmaking gifts, stepping onto it, binding hands) only where sourced
Church section covering Orthodox and Ukrainian Greek Catholic rites (crowning) from official church sources; 'ask your parish priest' for requirements

Travel note from Smartraveller only: 'Do not travel', updated 02 November 2026; embassy cannot give in-person consular or passport services; dual nationality lines quoted as Smartraveller gives them; no suggestion to marry in Ukraine
Bringing the customs to a wedding in Australia or another destination (diaspora angle), Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' for recognition only
FAQ of 5 to 7 questions with no amounts

tradition_plan.note: Planner (wedding-planner-sme) runs batch A and batch B in parallel, scratch folders 02-research/batch-a and 02-research/batch-b, 15 min HARD by the clock, save after every 3 facts, no extra sourcing rounds. Preferred sources: encyclopediaofukraine.com (Internet Encyclopedia of Ukraine), ich.unesco.org, Ukrainian Catholic Church official pages (ugcc.ua, Ukrainian Catholic Eparchy of Saints Peter and Paul in Australia), Ukrainian Autocephalous / Orthodox Church in Australia official pages, Ukrainian museums and culture institutions (for example Ivan Honchar Museum, National Museum of Ukrainian Folk Decorative Art), Britannica, academic journals. Never competitor wedding sites, vendor blogs, Wikipedia, lifestyle magazines. Unsourced: 'often told', no meanings as fact, no [[VERIFY]] marker. Ukrainian terms transliterated as the source gives them. One honest framing line per section. Culture, not politics.
tradition_plan.count: 11 customs plus the travel and legal note (batch A: 6 customs; batch B: 5 customs plus travel/legal)
